_comment: Manifest of free macOS diagnostic/repair tools, installed via Homebrew (brew formula) or Homebrew Cask (brew-cask, for GUI apps). IMPORTANT PLATFORM NOTE: Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3/M4) can only boot Apple-signed macOS/RecoveryOS images — there is no equivalent of booting a generic Linux/Windows rescue USB (no Boot Camp, no arbitrary ISO boot, unlike Intel Macs). Entries tagged 'platformNote' below are Intel-only or limited on Apple Silicon; see CLAUDE.md's Boot & Recovery section for the Apple-Silicon-safe alternatives (Recovery Mode, Apple Diagnostics, DFU restore via Apple Configurator 2).

tools.name: smartmontools
tools.purpose: SMART health/attributes (smartctl) — most useful here for external/USB/SATA drives; Apple's own internal NVMe SSDs expose limited SMART data to third-party tools by design.

tools.name: GrandPerspective
tools.purpose: Open-source disk-usage visualizer — free alternative to the paid DaisyDisk.

tools.name: testdisk
tools.purpose: Partition-table recovery and file undelete (bundles PhotoRec).

tools.name: Stats
tools.purpose: Menu-bar system monitor — CPU, GPU, RAM, disk, network, sensors, battery. Free, open source (MIT) — the real alternative to the paid iStat Menus, not a stripped-down trial.

tools.name: htop
tools.purpose: Interactive process/resource monitor for the terminal.

tools.name: btop
tools.purpose: Modern resource monitor (CPU/mem/disk/net/proc in one view).

tools.name: iTerm2
tools.purpose: Open-source terminal replacement — nicer environment to run Claude Code in than Terminal.app.

tools.name: ClamAV
tools.purpose: CLI antivirus scanner. Run `freshclam` after install to fetch current definitions.

tools.name: Malwarebytes
tools.purpose: Free on-demand malware/PUP scanner for Mac.
tools.licenseNote: Free consumer edition; if this becomes a for-profit repair business rather than occasional resale prep, check Malwarebytes' business terms.

tools.name: mas
tools.purpose: Mac App Store CLI — script the reinstall of App-Store-sourced apps during a refurb.

tools.name: balenaEtcher
tools.purpose: Flashes an ISO/IMG to a USB drive with checksum verification.
tools.platformNote: Only useful for building non-macOS boot media (e.g. a Linux live USB) on an Intel Mac. An Apple Silicon Mac cannot boot the resulting media at all — see CLAUDE.md.

tools.name: Ventoy
tools.platformNote: Intel Mac only, and even there Startup Security Utility (from Recovery Mode) must be set to allow booting from external/untrusted media first. Not usable at all on Apple Silicon.

tools.name: Rescuezilla
tools.purpose: Full-disk imaging/cloning from a bootable live environment.
tools.platformNote: Intel Mac only — same Startup Security Utility caveat as Ventoy above. On Apple Silicon, use Time Machine or `asr` (built-in Apple Software Restore) for imaging instead.

builtinDiagnostics._comment: Ships with every Mac, zero cost. The Boot & Recovery entries here are the ones that actually work on Apple Silicon — check `uname -m` (arm64 vs x86_64) or the Apple menu > About This Mac before proposing any boot-media-based fix, since the two platforms diverge completely here.

commands.purpose: Exact model, chip, serial — confirms what the machine actually is before diagnosing further.
Checks (non-destructively) the boot volume's filesystem for errors; use verifyDisk for the whole disk.
Recent error/fault-level entries from the unified log — the journalctl/Event Viewer equivalent.
Thermal throttling state — useful for a 'runs hot and slows down' complaint.
Samples a hung/unresponsive process to see what it's stuck doing (built-in, like a lightweight Process Monitor trace).

bootAndRecovery.name: macOS Recovery Mode
bootAndRecovery.howTo: Intel: hold Cmd+R at startup. Apple Silicon: hold the Power button until "Loading startup options" appears, then choose Options.
bootAndRecovery.purpose: Reinstall macOS, Disk Utility, Terminal, Safari for support articles — the primary rescue environment on every Mac, including Apple Silicon.

bootAndRecovery.name: Apple Diagnostics
bootAndRecovery.howTo: Intel: hold D at startup. Apple Silicon: hold Power at startup until options appear, then Cmd+D.
bootAndRecovery.purpose: Free built-in hardware test (logic board, memory, etc.) — gives a reference code, no software to install.

bootAndRecovery.name: Safe Mode
bootAndRecovery.howTo: Intel: hold Shift at startup. Apple Silicon: hold Power until "Loading startup options," select the disk, then hold Shift and click "Continue in Safe Mode."
bootAndRecovery.purpose: Boots with minimal extensions/caches — isolates a boot problem caused by a third-party kernel extension or login item.

bootAndRecovery.name: DFU restore via Apple Configurator 2
bootAndRecovery.howTo: Free from the Mac App Store; requires a second Mac and the right cable.
bootAndRecovery.purpose: The Apple Silicon equivalent of a full firmware/OS nuke-and-reinstall, for a Mac that won't boot at all — there is no bootable-USB-rescue path on these machines, this is the real fallback.

bootAndRecovery.name: Migration Assistant
bootAndRecovery.howTo: Applications > Utilities, or from within Recovery Mode.
